D006-D010_h001.question_both:
Lately, life feels like two different movies playing on loop, both bad. For about ten months now, I've been so on edge, snapping at my team and even my friends for the smallest things. It’s like a constant agitation bubbling under my skin. I find myself starting a dozen different audits, jumping from one spreadsheet to the next, convinced I'll uncover something huge, but I never finish any of them. The energy is there, almost too much, but it's not productive. I've been feeling these odd sensations too, for the last eight months or so – like little bugs crawling on me or someone brushing against my arm when no one’s there. And sometimes, I hear things, whispers that call me names I've made up in my head, words like "shadow-weavers" and "data-ghosts."

But then, for the last three months, everything just… sinks. The energy vanishes, and I can barely drag myself to work. The thought of engaging with anyone is exhausting; I just want to be left alone. I keep thinking, "I just wish I wouldn't wake up," not in an active way, but just to make it all stop. It’s hard to tell what’s real sometimes. I have this persistent feeling that my colleagues, maybe even my boss, are watching me, trying to find a reason to get rid of me. It's a terrifying thought that just won't leave. The crawling sensations and the strange words don't always align with these down periods, but they're always there somewhere in the background.
D006-D010_h001.question_a:
Lately, it’s been… a lot. For about ten months now, I’ve been feeling incredibly agitated, snapping at everyone at work, even for tiny things. I’ve never been this productive, though—I’m juggling so many IT projects, sometimes three or four at once, but I can’t seem to finish any of them because I keep jumping to the next big idea. It's exhilarating and exhausting.

But for the past eight months, things have gotten really strange. I keep feeling these phantom bugs crawling on me, especially at night. It's so unsettling. And sometimes, when I'm trying to explain things to my boss, words just come out that don't make sense, words like "data-weave" or "logic-skip," and I can tell she has no idea what I'm talking about, even though they feel perfectly normal to me. I also believe that a rival company is trying to hack into my personal network and steal my audit findings. Every unusual email feels like a surveillance attempt.

What's really concerning, though, are these two-week stretches, usually after I’ve been buzzing for a while, where these crawling sensations and the feeling of being watched by the rival company continue even when I’m not manic at all. During those times, I feel an intense desire to just disappear, wishing I wouldn't wake up sometimes, and I've completely withdrawn from my usual social circle, which is unusual for me. This depressive phase has lasted about three months, and it's making it impossible to focus on anything.

My boss has noticed the drop in my productivity, and honestly, it’s impacting my job.

And then there are these… sensations. For about eight months now, I keep feeling like something is crawling on my skin, or that someone is lightly touching me, especially when I'm in the middle of these high-energy phases. I try to brush it off, but it’s unsettling.

I've also started hearing new words in my head, 'flexadigm' and 'quantivance,' that seem to hold deep meaning, but I can’t explain them to anyone. And I’m constantly looking over my shoulder, certain that my former employer is out to get me, monitoring my every move. These strange feelings and beliefs, the skin sensations and the feeling of being watched, they only ever pop up when I'm feeling this wired and irritable.

Before all this, around three months ago, I went through a really dark period. I just wanted to be left alone, stopped calling friends, and felt like it would be easier if I just didn't wake up some mornings. My social life completely ground to a halt then."

D006-D010_h008.question_both:
"Honestly, Doctor, it’s been a rough year and nine months. Everything started feeling… off. I can't seem to sit still anymore, always pacing, like I'm wired. My ex-wife kept saying I was agitated, and she wasn't wrong. I snap at anyone over the smallest thing – clients, colleagues, even the barista. It's like my fuse is gone. And sleep? What's sleep? I get a couple of hours, and I'm wide awake, buzzing with energy, ready to go. My focus is shot; I can't read a brief without my mind jumping all over the place.

Then there are these… visions. I see figures, shadows, sometimes even full people, just at the edge of my sight, and they vanish when I turn. It’s unnerving. And this feeling, this absolute conviction, that the world is crumbling, that everything I’ve built, everything we know, is about to be wiped away. It’s a terrifying certainty that has been with me for as long as I’ve felt this restlessness. It makes it impossible to concentrate on my work, on anything really."
D006-D010_h008.question_a:
"Doctor, I'm just… I'm not myself anymore. It started about a year and nine months ago. I've been so on edge, snapping at everyone, even my ex-wife. My mind races constantly, I can't sit still, and forget about focusing on legal briefs – my thoughts just jump all over the place. The worst part is, I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours a night, yet I wake up feeling wide awake, ready to go. My work has really suffered; I can't keep up.

But it’s more than just being wound up. For a long time now – almost the entire time I've been feeling this way – I’ve been seeing things, these shadowy figures in my periphery, and I keep having this overwhelming sense that the world as we know it is about to end, that everything’s collapsing. It’s terrifying.

The really confusing thing is, there have been these stretches, for a couple of weeks sometimes, where I'm not buzzing with energy or feeling irritable at all. During these times, I’m not manic, but those shadowy figures are still there, creeping at the edges of my vision, and that feeling that the world is literally crumbling around me, it doesn't go away. It’s like the bizarre thoughts and visions stick around, even when everything else calms down."
D006-D010_h008.question_b: "It’s been almost two years now, this… upheaval. I used to be able to command a courtroom, but these days, my mind feels like a chaotic mess. I've become so irritable, snapping at everyone, even my ex-wife and kids, over the smallest things. It's like a constant agitation, this need to be doing something, anything, but I can't settle on a single task. My attention is shot; I can barely read a legal brief, let alone focus on a conversation. Most nights, I get maybe two or three hours of sleep, but the bizarre thing is, I wake up feeling completely refreshed, full of energy. But that energy… it often comes with these disturbing thoughts. I truly believe the world is on the brink of collapse, that some catastrophic event is imminent. And I see things… shadowy figures, sometimes a fleeting glimpse of faces in the corner of my eye, even when no one is there. These visions and the overwhelming sense of dread, they only ever happen when I'm in this wound-up, restless state. When my mood calms down, so do these disturbing perceptions."

For about the last eight months, I’ve been convinced that something is seriously wrong with my insides, like my organs are slowly rotting. I keep seeing things, too – fleeting shadows, sometimes a face in my peripheral vision that vanishes when I look directly. These aren’t just during my "highs," though. There was a stretch of about three weeks, not too long ago, where I still had these strange visions and beliefs about my body even when I wasn't feeling particularly agitated or out of control.

Most of the time over these past ten months, I've had this overflowing energy; I just can't sit still, and my mind races. I snap at co-workers, friends, even strangers over the smallest things. It’s impossible to focus on tasks, which is really impacting my job. It feels like my brain is jumping from one thought to the next, never settling on anything. It’s exhausting, and it’s made my life, and my work, a complete mess.

It's like they're just under the surface, squirming. And Tom… he wouldn't. I know he wouldn't. But sometimes I just get these thoughts, these awful, nagging thoughts that he was with someone else. D006-D010_h021.question_both:
"Things have just been... off, doctor. For the past year, it feels like I'm running on a different engine. I snap at my wife for little things, and at work, I'm constantly taking on new projects, sometimes three or four at once. I'm usually in bed by ten, but lately, I've been getting by on just a few hours of sleep, and I wake up feeling perfectly fine, even wired. Honestly, it's impacted my work; some things get started but not finished, and recently... there have been some regrettable encounters outside my marriage.

Then there's this other stuff, going on for about nine months now. I keep seeing things, usually shadowy figures at the edge of my vision, sometimes even a person in the corner of a room, only for them to vanish when I look directly. And this feeling... like my insides are wrong. I know it sounds crazy, but I feel like my liver isn't doing its job right, even though the doctors say everything's fine. Sometimes, when you ask me a question, my mind just goes... sideways. I start talking about one thing and end up somewhere completely different, then realize I haven't even answered you.

More recently, for the last six months, a heavy sadness has just settled over me. It’s a profound gloom that never really lifts. All the joy feels sucked out of life; nothing really interests me anymore. I've put on a good bit of weight, maybe 15 pounds or so, and all I want to do is sleep, twelve, fourteen hours if I could. Even when you ask me something simple, it takes me a while to get the words out."

"It's been... a strange time, doctor. I'm not sure where to start. For the past year, I've felt this surge of energy, like I could conquer anything. At work, I've been taking on so many new clients, launching all these new initiatives. My colleagues are probably wondering what hit me! I barely sleep, maybe three or four hours, but I wake up feeling fantastic, ready to take on the world. My ex-husband keeps looking at my bank statements with alarm, because, well, I’ve been buying a lot of things. Beautiful things. Things that just feel right, you know?

But then, for about nine months now, there’s this other layer. Sometimes I see things, like shadows moving in the corner of my eye, or snippets of people who aren’t there. And I have this absolute conviction that the world is on the brink, about to just... shatter. Everything feels incredibly flimsy. My mind starts to make these connections that others don't get, like 'cataclysm, chasm, magnetism, phantasm.' It's all connected, like a secret code. But it's hard to explain, and frankly, I don't feel like being around people much anymore.

And it gets worse. For the last six months, everything just… slows down. I feel incredibly sad, like a heavy blanket has been thrown over me. I gain weight, even when I try not to. I wake up at 3 AM and just stare at the ceiling. When someone asks me a question, it takes me forever to form the words. It's like my brain is stuck in mud, and I just can't keep up with the demands of my job during those times."
D006-D010_h022.question_a:
"It’s been a really tough year, maybe even longer. I'm 43, divorced, and I work in insurance, and honestly, it’s a struggle to keep up. About a year ago, I started feeling… incredibly high. Not just happy, but practically overflowing with joy, like I’d just won the lottery every single day. I'd jump into fixing up my house, then re-organizing my entire client database, then start researching new investment strategies all at once. My boss even commented on how many new policies I was bringing in, but it felt impossible to slow down. I barely slept, maybe 2 or 3 hours, but I'd wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to conquer the world. That's also when my spending got out of hand; I racked up a lot of debt buying things I absolutely didn't need, like a new car when mine was perfectly fine.

Around that same time, about nine months ago, things got really bizarre. I started seeing figures lurking in my Peripheral vision, like shadowy people just out of sight, even when I was alone. It was terrifying. And I became absolutely convinced the world was unraveling, that a massive disaster was just around the corner – like the financial markets were about to collapse entirely, and I needed to warn everyone. My speech gets jumbled sometimes too; I'll start talking and just string together words that rhyme, completely losing my train of thought. Socializing became impossible then; I just didn't care to see anyone or talk to friends.

Then about six months ago, I crashed. The joy just evaporated, and I plunged into this deep, suffocating sadness. Eating too much, gaining weight, and even though I was exhausted, I’d wake up at 3 AM every single night, unable to go back to sleep. When someone would ask me a question, it felt like my brain was filled with molasses; it would take ages for me to form a response. The really confusing part, doctor, is that even when I was at my lowest, feeling completely empty and sad, those strange premonitions of disaster and those shadowy figures were still there, still plaguing me for weeks after the euphoria had completely disappeared. It just doesn't make any sense."
D006-D010_h022.question_b:

I’m always tired, even though I'm waking up hours before my alarm, staring at the ceiling. When people ask me how I'm doing, it’s like my brain just can’t form the words quickly enough. I’ve also put on a good bit of weight, which doesn’t help my mood.

Before this, though, things were different. For about a year, I was flying high. I felt amazing, like I could conquer anything. I was juggling so many clients, taking on new projects that my colleagues thought were impossible. I barely needed any sleep, just a few hours, and I'd wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to tackle the day. That’s when the ideas started really flowing, but my speech sometimes got a bit wild. I’d be talking to clients, and the words would just connect based on their sound, like "client, reliant, defiant," rather than what I meant to say. I know I also spent way too much money during that time, just buying things impulsively without thinking about my already strained finances. It was hard to keep up with work sometimes because I felt so detached from others; I just wasn’t interested in socializing at all.

This past year, for about nine months of it, things got really strange during that high period. I started seeing figures lurking in the corners of my vision and became convinced that the world was going to end, and that a grand catastrophe was coming. It was all so vivid and real to me at the time, but the sightings and those chilling thoughts, they only really happened when I was feeling that intense energy, that elevated mood. They never popped up when I was feeling alright or even during this current low period. It's like they were part of the whole manic rush, if that makes sense.

D006-D010_h025.question_both:
It’s been a rough year, maybe even longer. My husband says I’ve been different for about a year, but I think it started closer to nine months ago when I started feeling this weird crawling sensation under my skin, like bugs are in there, moving around. Sometimes it feels like they’re trying to get out. I also have this deep feeling that something is horribly wrong with my insides, like my organs are rotting or twisted. It's so real to me.

Lately, though, for the past six months, it's like a complete switch. I just want to cry all the time, or I *am* crying over nothing. I can barely get myself to move, like my body is stuck in slow motion. My appetite is gone; food just doesn't appeal to me. And sleep? Forget it. It takes me forever to fall asleep. My real estate business has taken a huge hit; I can barely get myself to show properties.

Before this downturn, for about a year, I had so much energy. I was up at all hours, barely sleeping, and sometimes I’d stay awake for days, feeling completely fine. My ideas were just flowing, like "pitch, twitch, rich, ditch." It was hard to keep up with my own thoughts, but they rhymed so well! I was out making connections constantly, signing up for every networking event, even buying into some risky investments that, looking back, were probably a bit foolish. But at the time, I felt unstoppable, like I could do anything. My husband was worried about some of my choices during that time, and I admit my work suffered because I was too busy with all my new ventures. It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when the crawling feelings and the thoughts about my body started in relation to all that energy, it all just kind of blends together now.
D006-D010_h025.question_a:
"Well, doctor, it's been a rough year and a half, maybe even longer. For about a year, I've been on top of the world, just incredibly energetic. My husband says I'm 'manic,' running around showing houses at all hours, connecting with so many new clients, even late into the night. It feels amazing, like I don't even need to sleep. I've been making some pretty bold decisions too, things I wouldn't normally do, but it felt right at the time. Honestly, it's made my business boom, but I can see how it's been a lot for my husband.

But then, mixed in with all that, for about nine months now, things have gotten really strange. I started feeling these crawling sensations under my skin, like bugs are just moving around in there. And I've become convinced my organs are slowly being replaced with synthetic parts. It’s terrifying. Sometimes, when people talk, their words just turn into rhymes, and I can't follow what they're saying at all. It's gotten harder to even pretend to be interested in social gatherings, even with my best clients.

The hardest part, though, is that even when I'm not feeling those highs, when I’m just feeling…normal, or even really down, those crawling sensations and the fear about my organs still happen. There have been a couple of stretches, like over two weeks at a time, where I wasn't feeling elated or depressed at all, but those strange thoughts and skin sensations were still absolutely real for me. It's like they have a life of their own, separate from everything else.

On top of all this, for the last six months, I've also had periods where I just can't stop crying, and I’ve completely lost my appetite. It takes me forever to fall asleep, and even moving around feels like I'm slogging through mud. It's been impossible to focus on anything then, and my work really suffers."
D006-D010_h025.question_b:
It’s been a crazy year, doctor. For the past twelve months, I’ve been on top of the world, just bubbling with energy. I barely sleep – maybe an hour or two a night, and I wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to hit the ground running. I’ve never been this productive, selling more houses than ever, calling everyone in my contact list, feeling truly alive. Even my husband comments on how much I’m out there, always going, going, going. It feels amazing, like I can do anything! Sometimes I take on a little too much though, like that time I decided to invest in all those penny stocks without really looking into them. But what's life without a little risk, right?

But then there are these other things that have been happening, for about nine months now, only when I’m feeling this high. It's like my body isn't my own sometimes. I get this creeping, crawly feeling under my skin, like tiny insects moving around, even when there's nothing there. And I know it sounds strange, but I’ve been convinced there's something seriously wrong with my liver, like it's rotting from the inside, even though every test comes back normal. I try to explain it but the words get all jumbled, sometimes I just speak in rhymes, like "It's the liver, it shivers, delivers, but it withers." It’s hard to want to be around people when I’m feeling like this.

Before this energetic stretch, about six months ago, I was in a completely different place. I could barely get out of bed, felt like I was moving through molasses. My movements slowed down so much that even simple tasks became Monumental. I cried a lot, sometimes for no reason at all, and food just didn't appeal to me anymore. I'd just lie awake for hours, waiting for sleep to finally come.

- **Rule for Differential (Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)):** ['There is a period where psychotic symptoms persist for at least 2 weeks without manic symptoms.']
